books.title: Twenty Years After
books.author: Alexandre Dumas
books.desc: Twenty years on, d'Artagnan and the three musketeers find themselves on opposite sides of a civil war in France and a revolution in England.
about: In 1648 Cardinal Richelieu is dead and France is ruled by the regent Anne of Austria and her unpopular minister, Cardinal Mazarin, while the revolt of the Fronde stirs Paris. D'Artagnan, still a lieutenant of musketeers after twenty years, is sent by Mazarin to find his old companions. But Athos, now raising his ward Raoul, and Aramis, now an abbé, have chosen the other side, and only Porthos, rich and bored, agrees to join him. Across the Channel, King Charles I is fighting for his throne, and a dangerous young man named Mordaunt seeks revenge for the past.

Dumas mixes swordplay, escapes, disguises and humour with real history, from the barricades of Paris to the English Civil War, and shows the four friends older, wiser and tested by divided loyalties. Friendship ultimately proves stronger than politics.

Twenty Years After was published in instalments in the newspaper Le Siècle from January to August 1845, as the sequel to The Three Musketeers, written with the collaboration of Auguste Maquet. This edition offers the original French text and an English translation by an unnamed translator.

books.title: The Mysterious Island
books.author: Jules Verne
books.desc: Five Union prisoners escape the Civil War in a balloon and crash on an unknown Pacific island, where they build a new life, helped by a mysterious protector.
about: In March 1865, during the American Civil War, five Northern prisoners escape from Confederate Richmond in a balloon: the engineer Cyrus Harding, the journalist Gideon Spilett, the sailor Pencroft, the young Herbert and Harding's devoted servant Neb, together with his dog Top. Swept away by a hurricane, they come down on an unknown volcanic island in the Pacific, which they name Lincoln Island. With nothing but their knowledge and hard work, they set out to make it their home, while strange events suggest they are not alone.

Verne celebrates human ingenuity and cooperation as the castaways make fire, bricks, iron, glass and even electricity from what they find. The novel combines a detailed survival story with mystery and adventure, and links up with characters from his earlier novels Twenty Thousand Leagues Under the Seas and In Search of the Castaways.

The Mysterious Island was serialised in Hetzel's Magasin d'éducation et de récréation and published in book form in 1875, as one of Verne's Extraordinary Voyages. This edition offers the original French text and an English translation; in it Cyrus Smith of the French original is called Cyrus Harding.

books.title: Salammbô
books.author: Gustave Flaubert
books.desc: In ancient Carthage, rebellious mercenaries besiege the city, and their leader Matho becomes obsessed with Salammbô, the priestess daughter of Hamilcar.
about: After the First Punic War, Carthage cannot pay the mercenaries who fought for it. During a riotous feast in the gardens of the general Hamilcar Barca, the Libyan giant Matho sees Hamilcar's daughter Salammbô, a priestess of the moon goddess Tanith, and falls under her spell. Guided by the cunning former slave Spendius, Matho steals the goddess's sacred veil, and the mercenaries' revolt turns into a merciless war against the city.

Flaubert recreates the ancient world with dazzling, exotic and often brutal detail, from temples and palaces to battles and sieges. The novel is a sensuous and violent tale of passion, religion and war, drawn largely from the account of the Mercenary War by the Greek historian Polybius.

Salammbô was published in 1862 and was very popular. It is set in Carthage during the Mercenary War of 241–237 BC. This edition offers the original French text and an English translation by an unnamed translator.

books.title: Colomba
books.author: Prosper Mérimée
books.desc: A young Corsican officer comes home to find his fierce sister determined that he will avenge their murdered father, in Mérimée's tale of vendetta.
about: Returning home to Corsica after serving in Napoleon's army, the young lieutenant Orso della Rebbia travels on the same ship as an English colonel, Sir Thomas Nevil, and his romantic daughter Lydia, who is fascinated by tales of bandits and vendettas. In his village, Orso is welcomed by his sister Colomba, a passionate young woman convinced that their father was murdered by the rival Barricini family, and determined that her brother will take revenge.

Mérimée paints the landscapes, customs and code of honour of Corsica with sharp, ironic precision, contrasting the civilised visitors with the fierce traditions of the island. Colomba herself, proud and implacable, is one of his most memorable heroines.

Colomba first appeared in the Revue des deux Mondes on 1 July 1840, after Mérimée had visited Corsica in 1839 as inspector of historical monuments. This edition offers the original French text and the English translation by Lady Mary Loyd.

books.title: The Government Inspector
books.author: Nikolai Gogol
books.desc: In a corrupt provincial town, the panicking officials mistake a penniless young clerk from St Petersburg for a government inspector travelling incognito.
about: The Mayor of a small Russian town gathers his officials with alarming news: a government inspector is on his way from St Petersburg, travelling incognito. Every one of them has something to hide. When two local gossips report that a mysterious young man has been staying at the inn for two weeks without paying, they decide he must be the inspector. The young man, Khlestakov, a frivolous minor clerk who has gambled away his money, is only too happy to accept their hospitality, their bribes and the attentions of the Mayor's wife and daughter.

Gogol's comedy is a merciless satire of bureaucracy, bribery, vanity and fear, in which every character is shown up by the misunderstanding. Its epigraph, "Don't blame the mirror if your face is crooked", sums up its intention.

The play was first performed at the Alexandrinsky Theatre in St Petersburg in 1836, with the support of Tsar Nicholas I, and it caused great controversy. Pushkin is said to have given Gogol the idea for its plot. This English translation, titled The Inspector-General, is by Thomas Seltzer.
